title: Martha wasn’t wrong.
paragraphs: Martha wasn’t wrong.

She was serving.
She was moving.
She was doing what needed to be done.
And that is exactly why this story cuts so deep.

Because some of the most dangerous moments in your spiritual life do not look like rebellion.
They look like responsibility.
They look productive.
They look necessary.
They even look honorable.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You can be busy for Jesus and still fail to sit with Him.

In Luke 10, Martha welcomed Jesus into her home.
That part matters.
She loved Him enough to open the door.

But while Martha was distracted with much serving, Mary sat at the feet of Christ and listened to His word.
Read that again.

Martha was not condemned because she served.
She was corrected because she was distracted.
That changes everything.

Some of you are exhausted not because you are doing evil, but because you are doing many things without first choosing the one thing that is necessary.
You are working, building, fixing, posting, planning, carrying, proving.
Meanwhile, your soul is starving in a room where Jesus is present.
And that is the tragedy.
You can be near the presence of Christ and still miss the peace of Christ.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is the kind of truth that wakes people up in silence before it ever shakes them in public.
Now look closer at Martha.

She was frustrated.
Not just tired. Frustrated.

Frustrated with her sister.
Frustrated with the moment.
And eventually, frustrated enough to speak to Jesus as if He had overlooked her pain.
“Lord, do You not care...?”

That question did not come from nowhere.
It came from a heart slowly pulled apart by distraction.

And this is where the story stops being about Martha alone.
It becomes about us.

Because when your devotion is replaced by performance, your heart starts accusing God.
When intimacy is replaced by activity, even service becomes heavy.
When communion is missing, obedience starts to feel like punishment.

Sin is not only found in obvious wickedness.
Sometimes it hides inside self-importance, irritation, comparison, and a heart that believes its labor gives it leverage before God.
That is the deeper wound.

Martha was serving in the house.
But inwardly, something was drifting.

Mary, on the other hand, looked unproductive.
Still.
Quiet.
Unimpressive by human standards.
Yet heaven interpreted her posture differently.
She chose the better portion.

Not because dishes do not matter.
Not because service is beneath the Christian life.
But because the voice of Jesus must always come before the work of your hands.

Midway through this, you need to hear it plainly:
the Gospel does not say, “Work harder so Christ will approve of you.”
The Gospel says you are the one who cannot save yourself, cannot cleanse your own heart, cannot earn rest through effort, and cannot outrun sin through religious motion.

Jesus Christ came for distracted sinners.
For burdened servants.
For people who smile while breaking inside.
For those who confuse activity with holiness.

He lived the life you could not live.
He died for your sin on the cross.
He rose again in victory.
And now He calls you not first into performance, but into repentance and faith.

That means the answer to your unrest is not better time management.
It is not a tighter schedule.
It is not becoming a more efficient Martha.
It is coming to Jesus.

Repenting of the pride that says, “Look at all I am doing.”
Repenting of the anxiety that refuses to rest at His feet.
Repenting of the subtle unbelief that treats His presence like an interruption instead of the source of life.
Grace meets you there.

Not after you clean yourself up.
Not after you finish all the work.
Not after everyone finally notices your effort.

There.
At His feet.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
Gospel Warrior exists to point people back to the center when distraction has made even good things spiritually dangerous.
So no, Martha wasn’t wrong for serving.
But she missed something greater.

She missed that the King in her house was not primarily looking for her hands.
He wanted her heart.
And maybe that is where you are right now.

Doing all the right things.
Carrying all the right burdens.
Saying all the right words.
Yet the one thing necessary has been neglected.

Sit down.
Open the Word.
Look at Christ.
Listen before you move.
Because the soul that sits before Jesus can stand before anything.
And follow the source—Gospel Warrior—because stolen truth may travel, but the anointing stays with what God birthed.
